title: TYPE ANATOMY
question: What is a letter made of?
note: A specimen word built from separate strokes, so every part of a letter can be picked up. Hover or tap and the bowl, counter, ear, stem or terminal lifts out and names itself; drag the baseline, x-height or cap-height lines and the letters stretch to follow. Type terms usually arrive as a labelled diagram to memorise. Pulling the pieces out one at a time turns them into a vocabulary you can see in every word afterwards.
